exposure: The death of an infant aged 0 to 7 days following an unremarkable pregnancy owing to causes other than birth defects, accidents/assaults, or sudden infant death syndrome.
cohort: Live births in 477 US counties that experienced an unexpected newborn death during the study period (2011-2017)
finding: The study found mixed results regarding the association between unexpected newborn death and subsequent changes in obstetric and newborn procedures, with some models showing an increase in interventions like cesarean delivery and assisted ventilation, but not consistently across all models.
mod_finding: Following an unexpected newborn death, there was a significant increase in the probability of cesarean delivery in 3 out of 4 estimated models.
